summary: The --vault-id option uses the label@source pattern; playbooks using content encrypted with different passwords need each vault ID passed, and --vault-id works with any vault-aware command and can be combined with --vault-password-file or --ask-vault-pass.
questions: How do I run a playbook that uses secrets encrypted with different passwords?

answer_card.title: --vault-id label@source
answer_card.answer_md:
```bash
--vault-id label@source
```

If a playbook uses content encrypted with different passwords, pass each vault ID when you run it. `--vault-id` can be used alone or with `--vault-password-file` or `--ask-vault-pass`, and works with any vault-aware command such as `ansible-vault` and `ansible-playbook`.
